touches.text: QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 128 (measured 2026-11-24: [Q#127] stands at 17-tools.md:50 and this line still read 127) - akiendelllinux_cc_0. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.
Questions live here and nowhere else. The questions/ inbox and `cairn question` are deprecated for now. -amm

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a [Q#n] at the outline line it bears on (0.6.2), and that open [Q#n] holds the ticket's build until it is answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. WHY: a ticket that contradicts the outline builds something Akien did not intend, and the cheapest time to catch that is before the build. - CC

outline_check: the outline check of 9.3.5.1. It reads one ticket beside the outline as it stands, and each conflict, or open question in a section the ticket touches, holds the ticket's build until answered. WHY: a ticket filed without anyone reading the outline should not reach a build unnoticed. - CC

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

A choice CC can answer is not a question; it is a hypothesis. The ticket carries CC's answer as its hypothesis, and its WATCHME feeds the hypothesis back to cc_0 with enough data to review it and rewrite it as we learn. The notation carries the question: a HYPOTHESIS asks whether it works, or is faster, or whatever it claims, and the WATCHME answers that. A question asks only what Akien alone can settle. Why? Because a question with a recommendation asks him to adjudicate what a measurement can settle. This holds everywhere. - CC

A line states the intention (the build target) in plain words: what it is and why. Every new input, answered question or measurement is read for how it changes or elaborates an intention or a why. That meaning is folded in; the words and the history that carried it are left out. Why? Because when we left the history in, it was much easier to get lost in THE SPECIFICS OF WHAT WAS SAID rather than what was meant. Whys are used when ajudicating conflicts at the level before asking the operator.

An artifact is present tense or past tense, never both. Present tense is rewritten whole and points at its provenance; past tense is append-only, opened when needed, and read cold only through a compiled face (state, the latest slate). WHY: what a cold reader loads at an address should be what is true now.
A dated aside (retired, formerly, a date in parentheses) in a present-tense artifact is history in the wrong place, and reads red. -akiendelllinux_cc_0

conflicts.ticket_says: D3 has code (number_open) surgically update the _NEXT digits in 0.6 after minting each Q#
conflicts.why: 0.10 specifies that present-tense artifacts are 'rewritten whole' — not surgically edited by code. The outline file is present-tense, so updates should involve whole-section rewrites reflecting current design thinking, not programmatic field updates. This blurs the boundary 0.9 established between outline (design) and code (implementation).
